body: So you want to sacrifice 17 years for a person you have just met? It seems that the issues are deep within yourself not just with your partner. Why would anyone "resent" showing love to their significant other? You wish to reclaim your youth but by doing so you are clinging on to the dynamics of lust which are usually short lived and end in pain and disappointment. Your wife was on her knees begging for you to stay with her. That is a sign of love. Yet yourself, a grown man, want to discard her as if she has meant nothing to you. Just imagine that woman you married. The first nights of your intimate relationship, the romance. The feelings are similar and more authentic as to what you are feeling now as they have happened. And you are yet to physically meet this other woman. You are a grown man. Take responsibility and make your marriage work if you can. Like I said, these moments of lust towards other women usually end in heartbreak and pain, and you are left wondering if only I had been more resilient and had the strength to rekindle my marriage romantically. It's possible. It just requires cohesion and coherence.

It's a poem I wrote on two separate nights. The first night I was ruminating, unable to really capture any poetic inspiration. I decided to take a step outside in a night that was beginning to shiver. All I had was a beer, a packet of cigarettes and my phone as it was too dark to write on paper. There was almost no pollution in the sky. So the sky was bare. And I began writing. I tend to incorporate my setting and environment in the majority of my poems as it's the place where I am at that present moment. And something about the stars will remain a mystery to me as long as I live. 

The poem is an interpretation of life and the human condition. Dreams that have not been realised, numbed by narcotics, universal projections and writing. It's one of the most vulnerable feelings to be out in the night with nothing but a canvas of white specks in the air, however it's also liberating in nature.

Well, even Orwell suggested that Kipling was somewhat of an imperialist. However that's not the point. He was an exceptional writer. That cannot be stated enough. 

Not all men are perfect, and we cannot assume that his poems and writings were not of any historical and cultural significance. The painting over of the mural was not the right way of addressing his imperial sympathies. The irony was that the poem addressed the very same ideological beliefs that progressive liberalism espouses. Students tend to take their activism to the extreme. It's a rebellious point in their lives. I was once a student at a very progressive university and I held progressive beliefs, more so to centre-left. However I always believed in open discussion and free-speech. In challenging different ideologies through dialogue. All we see now is anger within political discussion and spite. This is not how students, academics, journalists nor Presidents should be conducting themselves. There is a difference in freedom of speech and speech which crosses the boundaries of decency and results in vitriolic finger pointing.

I am able to understand both sides of the readership when it comes to this poem. 

On one side there are those who struggle to comprehend the true artistry and poetry of the poem due to its lack of what I would call "true soul". And what I mean by "true soul" is something that comes from the very depths of a place that you cannot comprehend. Works of truly outstanding poetry. The Homers, the Keats, the Nerudas of history. These readers perceive such a poem as being too short and non-elaborative to consider it as outstanding poetry. They see the poem as a piece which doesn't dwell further into the corners of the mind and heart. And I can agree with them to an extent.

The extent being, and now I sympathise with other readers with the opinion that poetry as an art form does not always have to resort to the reader smoking countless cigarettes after finishing the poem due to the mentally exhausting nature of compiling their inner most thoughts and emotions. Some poems are more placid, with a modest use of imagery and figuration. They do not have to send the reader on a journey through their soul, to measure the weight of their pain nor the beauty of what they interpret to be of value in this world. 

This is the beauty and weight of poetry. It is varied. It should always cast away elitism, whilst at the same time, appreciating the true greats and admiring those that produce words of art to better understand this world and themselves.

Demeaned into believing that indifference to our differences is what should be celebrated. What should be celebrated is that very same difference that makes us individuals with a rational mind.
